title: DocDancer: Towards Agentic Document-Grounded Information Seeking

Prior work has demonstrated that large-scale agent-synthesized data can be effectively generated for search agents Wu et al. ( 2025a ); Li et al. ( 2025b ); Tao et al. ( 2025 ) , code agents Yang et al. ( 2025 ) , GUI agents Sun et al. ( 2025b ); Guo et al. ( 2025a ) and general-purpose agents Fang et al. ( 2025 ); Prabhakar et al. ( 2025 ) . In contrast, this work focuses on the DocQA agent setting. Existing DocQA datasets are primarily constructed through semi-automated Van Landeghem et al. ( 2023 ); Dong et al. ( 2025b ) or expert-annotated Hendrycks et al. ( 2021 ); Deng et al. ( 2025 ) processes, both of which require substantial human involvement or result in questions that lack sufficient depth. Inspired by advances in search agents, we formulate DocQA as an agentic information-seeking problem, with the goal of synthesizing high-quality training data tailored for DocQA agents. Framework. We adopt the vanilla ReAct (Yao et al. , 2022 ) as the agent’s framework, which synergizes reasoning and acting. In this paradigm, the agent generates both a reasoning trace (thought), τ \tau , and a subsequent action, a a , in an interleaved manner.
